entities.summary: Viscount Saitō Makoto  was a Japanese admiral and politician who was prime minister of Japan from 1932 to 1934. Upon distinguishing himself during his command of two cruisers in the First Sino-Japanese War, Saitō rose rapidly to the rank of rear admiral by 1900. He was promoted to vice admiral during the Russo-Japanese War in 1904. After serving as Minister of the Navy from 1906 to 1914, Saitō held the position of Governor-General of Korea from 1919 to 1927 and again from 1929 to 1931. When Inukai Tsuyoshi was assassinated in May 1932, he took his place as prime minister and served one term in office.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As prime minister of Japan from 1932 to 1934, Saitō Makoto's tenure was marked by significant regional impact, particularly in East Asia. His leadership during this period had far-reaching consequences for the region, including the establishment of Japan's dominance in Korea.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As prime minister of Japan from 1932 to 1934, Saitō Makoto played a significant role in shaping the country's foreign policy during a tumultuous period, including the aftermath of Inukai Tsuyoshi's assassination and the lead-up to World War II.
